exercises.name: Dead bug
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent above your hips and your shins parallel to the floor.
Reach both arms straight up toward the ceiling, directly above your shoulders.
Press your lower back gently into the floor so there is no gap under your waist.
Breathe out and slowly lower your right arm overhead while straightening your left leg toward the floor.
Stop before your lower back lifts. Breathe in and return to the start.
Alternate sides, moving slowly enough that the movement takes about four seconds each way.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Dead bug. Knees above hips. Extend the opposite arm and leg slowly, keeping your lower back down.
safety_notes: Stop lowering the leg the moment your lower back arches away from the floor.
Keep your neck relaxed; if it strains, rest your head on a folded towel.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back arch, which shifts the work off the deep abdominals.
Rushing the movement so momentum carries the limbs rather than control.

exercises.name: The hundred, preparation
how_to: Lie on your back, knees bent above your hips, arms long by your sides.
Curl your head, neck and shoulders slightly off the mat, looking toward your knees.
Hold your arms just off the floor and pulse them up and down in small movements.
Breathe in for five pulses and out for five pulses.
Keep your ribs drawing down toward your hips throughout.
exercises.spoken_instruction: The hundred. Curl your shoulders off the mat and pulse your arms, five counts in, five out.
safety_notes: If your neck tires, lower your head to the mat and keep pulsing the arms.
Keep the curl small; height is not the point.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck to lift higher.
Holding the breath instead of using the five-count rhythm.

exercises.name: Shoulder bridge
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Press through your heels and peel your hips off the mat one vertebra at a time.
Stop when your hips, knees and shoulders form a straight line.
Hold for two breaths, then lower slowly from the top of the spine down.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Shoulder bridge. Press through your heels and lift your hips, then lower one vertebra at a time.
safety_notes: Do not push the hips higher than a straight line; over-arching loads the lower back.
Keep your knees tracking over your ankles rather than falling inward.
common_mistakes: Lifting with the lower back instead of the glutes.
Letting the knees splay apart at the top.

exercises.name: Side plank from the knees
how_to: Lie on your side with your bottom forearm on the mat, elbow under your shoulder, and your knees bent behind you.
Stack your hips and shoulders so your body forms one line from head to knees.
Lift your hips away from the floor and hold, breathing evenly.
Lower with control and change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Side plank from the knees. Elbow under your shoulder, lift your hips into one straight line and hold.
safety_notes: Keep the supporting shoulder pressed down and away from your ear.
Come down if the shoulder or wrist starts to ache.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drift backward so the line breaks at the waist.
Sinking into the supporting shoulder.

exercises.name: Single leg stretch
how_to: Lie on your back and curl your head and shoulders slightly off the mat.
Draw one knee toward your chest and hold your shin, extending the other leg away at about 45 degrees.
Switch legs smoothly, keeping your torso still and your ribs drawing down.
Breathe out as each knee comes in.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Single leg stretch. Curl up, draw one knee in and extend the other leg away, then switch smoothly.
safety_notes: Extend the moving leg higher if your lower back lifts off the mat.
Support your head with one hand if your neck fatigues.
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso side to side as the legs change.
Dropping the extended leg so low that the back arches.

exercises.name: Reformer footwork, toes
how_to: Lie on the carriage with your head on the headrest and the balls of your feet on the footbar, heels together and toes apart.
Set a moderate spring load, typically two to three springs depending on your reformer.
Press the carriage away by straightening your legs, stopping just short of locking the knees.
Return slowly, letting the springs resist rather than pull you back.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Reformer footwork on the toes. Press the carriage away, stopping short of locking your knees, and return slowly.
safety_notes: Check the springs are attached before you load the carriage.
Keep your heels lifted and together; do not let the ankles roll outward.
common_mistakes: Snapping the knees straight at the end of the press.
Letting the carriage return faster than you can control.

exercises.name: Reformer leg circles in straps
how_to: Lie on the carriage with both feet in the straps and legs extended at about 45 degrees.
Use a light spring load so the work comes from your control rather than the springs.
Circle both legs outward and around, keeping your pelvis completely still.
Complete the set, then reverse the direction.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Leg circles in the straps. Circle both legs outward, keeping your pelvis still, then reverse.
safety_notes: Make the circles smaller if your pelvis rocks or your back arches.
Keep the straps under tension throughout so they cannot snap slack.
common_mistakes: Circling so wide that the lower back lifts.
Gripping the shoulders up toward the ears.

exercises.name: Elliptical steady state
how_to: Stand tall on the pedals with a light hold on the handles.
Set a resistance you can sustain while still able to speak in full sentences.
Keep a steady cadence and let your heels stay in contact with the pedals.
Aim for an effort of three to four out of ten.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Elliptical steady state. Settle into a pace you could hold a conversation at, around three to four out of ten.
safety_notes: Do not lean your body weight onto the handles; it reduces the work and strains the wrists.
Ease off if you feel light-headed.
common_mistakes: Choosing a resistance so low that the pedals carry you.
Bouncing the shoulders with each stride.

exercises.name: Elliptical hard interval
how_to: Raise the resistance one or two steps above your steady-state setting.
Drive the pedals with a strong, quick cadence.
Target an effort of eight to nine out of ten, where speaking is limited to a few words.
Hold the effort for the full interval, then drop back to an easy pace to recover.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Hard interval. Lift the resistance and drive hard, eight to nine out of ten.
safety_notes: Build up to hard intervals over two to three weeks rather than starting here.
Stop immediately if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Going so hard in the first interval that later ones collapse.
Cutting the recovery short, which flattens the whole set.

exercises.name: Seated flat road
how_to: Set the saddle so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit tall with your hands resting lightly on the bars.
Add enough resistance that the flywheel feels connected rather than spinning freely.
Hold a smooth cadence of roughly 80 to 90 revolutions per minute.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Seated flat road. Sit tall, smooth cadence around eighty to ninety.
safety_notes: Never pedal with no resistance; the flywheel will drive your legs faster than you can control.
Keep your knees tracking forward, not bowing outward.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Saddle set too low, which loads the front of the knee.
Gripping the bars hard enough to hunch the shoulders.

exercises.name: Seated climb
how_to: Increase the resistance until the cadence naturally drops to around 60 to 70.
Stay seated, hinge very slightly forward from the hips and keep your torso quiet.
Push through the whole pedal circle rather than stamping down.
Hold an effort of six to seven out of ten.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Seated climb. Add resistance and drive through the whole pedal stroke.
safety_notes: Reduce resistance if your hips start rocking side to side.
Keep breathing rhythmically; do not hold your breath through the hard part.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the bars to compensate for too much resistance.
Letting the cadence fall below 55, which grinds the knees.

exercises.name: Standing sprint
how_to: Keep a moderate resistance — enough to stand against, not so much that you stall.
Rise out of the saddle with your hips over the pedals and hands on the wide part of the bars.
Drive a fast, controlled cadence at an effort of nine out of ten.
Sit back down and spin easy as soon as the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Standing sprint. Out of the saddle, fast and strong, nine out of ten.
safety_notes: Do not stand with light resistance; you will lose control of the pedals.
Skip this movement entirely if you have knee or hip pain today.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the hips rather than staying centred over the pedals.
Holding the sprint past the point where form breaks down.

exercises.name: March in place
how_to: Stand tall and march on the spot, lifting each knee to about hip height.
Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your legs.
Build gradually from a walking pace to a brisk one over the interval.
exercises.spoken_instruction: March in place. Lift the knees and let the arms swing, building the pace gradually.
safety_notes: Hold a wall or chair if your balance is unsteady.
common_mistakes: Starting too fast, so the warm-up becomes the workout.

exercises.name: Supine knee hug
how_to: Lie on your back and draw both knees gently toward your chest.
Hold behind your thighs rather than over the front of your knees.
Breathe slowly and let your lower back settle into the mat.
Hold for the full interval without bouncing.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Supine knee hug. Draw both knees toward your chest and breathe slowly.
safety_notes: Ease off to a comfortable stretch; this should never be sharp.
common_mistakes: Pulling hard on the front of the knee joint.

exercises.name: Lateral breathing
how_to: Sit or lie comfortably and rest your hands on the sides of your lower ribs.
Breathe in through your nose and feel your ribs widen sideways into your hands.
Breathe out through your mouth and feel the ribs close and soften downward.
Keep your shoulders still throughout, so the movement happens in the ribs rather than the neck.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Lateral breathing. Feel your ribs widen sideways into your hands, then soften them down.
safety_notes: Breathe at a comfortable depth; stop if you feel light-headed.
common_mistakes: Lifting the shoulders on the in-breath instead of widening the ribs.
Forcing the breath so deep that the neck and jaw tighten.

exercises.name: Cat cow
how_to: Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Breathe out and round your spine upward, drawing your navel toward your spine.
Breathe in and reverse the curve, letting your chest open and your tailbone lift.
Move at the pace of your breath, taking about three seconds in each direction.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Cat cow. Round the spine as you breathe out, open the chest as you breathe in.
safety_notes: Move within a comfortable range; this should feel like articulation, never a pinch.
Put a folded towel under your knees if kneeling is uncomfortable.
common_mistakes: Moving only the lower back, so the mid-spine never articulates.
Locking the elbows and pushing through the wrists.

exercises.name: Supine spine twist
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, arms out to the sides.
Keep your shoulders on the mat and let both knees drop slowly to one side.
Stop as soon as the opposite shoulder wants to lift, then return through the middle.
Alternate sides, breathing out as the knees travel.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Supine twist. Let both knees drop to one side, keeping both shoulders on the mat.
safety_notes: Stop the rotation before the opposite shoulder lifts; forcing it loads the lower back.
Keep the movement slow — never let the legs swing.
common_mistakes: Letting the top shoulder peel off the mat to get more range.
Using momentum instead of control to change sides.

exercises.name: Heel slides
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Find a neutral pelvis, so your lower back is neither arched nor flattened hard into the mat.
Slide one heel slowly away along the floor until the leg is nearly straight.
Stop the moment your pelvis wants to tip, then slide the heel back and change legs.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Heel slides. Slide one heel away along the floor while your pelvis stays completely still.
safety_notes: Shorten the slide as soon as your pelvis tips or your back arches.
common_mistakes: Sliding so far that the pelvis tilts, which moves the work off the deep abdominals.
Holding the breath while the leg travels.

exercises.name: Bird dog
how_to: Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and a long, level spine.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Hold for two breaths without letting your hips tilt or your back arch.
Return slowly and change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Bird dog. Reach the opposite arm and leg long, keeping your hips level.
safety_notes: Lift the limbs only as high as you can keep the pelvis level.
Come down if the supporting wrist begins to ache.
common_mistakes: Lifting the leg higher than the hip, which arches the lower back.
Letting the hips rotate toward the lifted leg.

exercises.name: Clam
how_to: Lie on your side with your knees bent and stacked, and your heels in line with your spine.
Rest your head on your lower arm and keep your hips stacked vertically.
Keep your heels together and open the top knee as far as it goes without the pelvis rolling back.
Lower the knee slowly and repeat, then change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Clam. Heels together, open the top knee without letting your pelvis roll backward.
safety_notes: Reduce the range as soon as the hip you are lying on starts to ache.
common_mistakes: Rolling the top hip backward to open the knee further.
Letting the heels separate, which turns it into a different movement.

exercises.name: Forearm plank
how_to: Set your forearms on the mat with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body forms one line from the crown of your head to your heels.
Draw your ribs down and your tailbone slightly under so the lower back does not dip.
Breathe evenly and hold; lower your knees the moment the line breaks.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Forearm plank. One straight line from head to heels, ribs drawing down.
safety_notes: Drop to your knees as soon as your hips sag; holding a broken plank loads the lower back.
Keep your shoulders pressed away from your ears.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag, which shifts the load onto the lower back.
Lifting the hips high to make the hold easier.

exercises.name: Swimming, preparation
how_to: Lie face down with your arms reaching overhead and your forehead resting on the mat.
Lengthen the back of your neck and draw your navel gently away from the floor.
Lift one arm and the opposite leg a few centimetres, keeping both long.
Lower them and change sides, moving smoothly rather than lifting high.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Swimming preparation. Lift the opposite arm and leg a little, staying long through the spine.
safety_notes: Keep the lift small; height is not the point and a big lift compresses the lower back.
Place a folded towel under your hips if your back feels crowded.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest and legs high, which shortens the lower back.
Letting the head drop back so the neck extends.

exercises.name: Double leg stretch
how_to: Lie on your back, curl your head and shoulders off the mat and hug both knees in.
Breathe in and reach your arms overhead while extending both legs away at an angle.
Stop extending the moment your lower back lifts off the mat.
Breathe out and circle your arms around to hug the knees back in.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Double leg stretch. Reach arms and legs long, then circle the arms round and hug the knees in.
safety_notes: Keep the legs higher than feels natural if your lower back lifts.
Lower your head to the mat if your neck fatigues, and keep the leg work going.
common_mistakes: Extending the legs so low that the back arches.
Letting the shoulders drop back to the mat mid-movement.

exercises.name: Criss cross
how_to: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and elbows wide.
Curl your head and shoulders off the mat and bring one knee in, extending the other leg away.
Rotate your ribcage toward the bent knee, leading with the shoulder rather than the elbow.
Switch sides slowly, keeping the curl height constant.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Criss cross. Rotate the ribs toward the bent knee, leading with the shoulder.
safety_notes: Never pull on your head with your hands; the hands only support the weight of the skull.
Reduce the rotation if your neck rather than your waist is doing the work.
common_mistakes: Yanking the elbow across instead of rotating the ribcage.
Dropping the curl between sides so the abdominals rest.

exercises.name: Roll up
how_to: Lie on your back with your legs long and your arms reaching overhead.
Breathe out and curl your head, then your shoulders, then your spine off the mat one section at a time.
Reach forward over your legs at the top, keeping your spine rounded.
Roll back down just as slowly, placing each part of the spine on the mat in turn.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Roll up. Peel the spine off the mat one section at a time, then lower just as slowly.
safety_notes: Bend your knees slightly if your lower back or hamstrings pull.
If you cannot roll down with control, stop partway rather than dropping.
common_mistakes: Throwing the arms to build momentum through the sticky part.
Losing the rounded spine so the movement becomes a flat-backed sit-up.

exercises.name: Shoulder bridge with march
how_to: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet flat, and lift your hips into a shoulder bridge.
Hold the bridge with your hips, knees and shoulders in one line.
Lift one foot a few centimetres off the mat without letting the hips drop or tilt.
Replace it and lift the other, marching slowly while the pelvis stays level.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Bridge with march. Hold the hips level and lift one foot at a time, slowly.
safety_notes: Lower the bridge if the hips drop or tilt when a foot lifts.
Keep the weight in your shoulders and heels, not your neck.
common_mistakes: Letting one hip drop as the foot lifts.
Pushing the hips so high that the lower back over-arches.

exercises.name: Side kick series
how_to: Lie on your side in one long line, propped on your forearm with your hips stacked.
Lift the top leg to hip height and keep it long and turned neither in nor out.
Swing the leg forward as far as your pelvis stays still, then sweep it back behind the line of your body.
Keep the torso completely quiet, then change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Side kick. Swing the top leg forward and back while your torso stays completely still.
safety_notes: Shorten the swing as soon as the pelvis rocks or the back arches.
Rest your head on your arm if the supporting shoulder aches.
common_mistakes: Swinging so far that the pelvis rolls with the leg.
Letting the waist collapse toward the mat.

exercises.name: Slow mountain climber
how_to: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and one long line from head to heels.
Draw one knee slowly toward your chest without letting your hips lift or your back round.
Return the foot to the floor and change legs at a controlled pace.
Keep your shoulders directly over your wrists throughout.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Slow mountain climber. Draw one knee in at a time while your hips stay level.
safety_notes: Drop to your knees if your hips start to pike or sag.
Come out of the position if your wrists hurt rather than working through it.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the hips upward as each knee comes in.
Letting the shoulders drift behind the wrists.

exercises.name: Teaser, preparation
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your arms reaching toward your feet.
Curl your head and shoulders up and lift both feet so your shins are parallel to the floor.
Roll a little further up onto the back of your pelvis, keeping your spine rounded into a shallow V.
Hold for two breaths, then lower the spine and the legs together with control.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Teaser preparation. Balance on the back of your pelvis in a shallow V, spine rounded.
safety_notes: Keep your knees bent until you can lower with full control.
Stop if the lower back takes over from the abdominals.
common_mistakes: Straightening the legs before the abdominals can hold the position.
Dropping out of the shape rather than lowering through it.

exercises.name: Full side plank
how_to: Lie on your side with your forearm on the mat and your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Stack your feet and lift your hips so your body forms one line from head to heels.
Press the supporting shoulder down and lengthen the top side of your waist.
Hold, breathing evenly, then lower with control and change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Full side plank. Feet stacked, hips lifted into one line, supporting shoulder pressed down.
safety_notes: Return to the knees version the moment your hips sag.
Come down if the supporting shoulder or wrist starts to ache.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drift back so the body folds at the waist.
Collapsing into the supporting shoulder.

exercises.name: Jack knife
how_to: Lie on your back with your arms pressing into the mat beside you and your legs extended upward.
Lower your legs a little, then lift your hips so your legs travel over your head and your weight moves onto your shoulders.
Extend your legs upward from there, keeping the weight off your neck.
Roll down through the spine slowly until your hips reach the mat.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Jack knife. Lift the hips and extend the legs upward, weight in the shoulders, not the neck.
safety_notes: Never let weight land on your neck; if it does, come down immediately.
Skip this movement entirely if you have any neck complaint today.
Keep the roll-down slow — dropping out of it loads the spine sharply.
common_mistakes: Throwing the legs overhead so the weight lands on the neck.
Rolling down in one piece instead of one vertebra at a time.

exercises.name: Star jumps
how_to: Stand tall with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump your feet wide while sweeping your arms overhead, landing softly through the whole foot.
Jump back to the start, keeping your knees soft and tracking over your toes.
Keep the rhythm steady and land quietly rather than heavily.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Star jumps. Land softly through the whole foot, knees tracking over your toes.
safety_notes: Step the feet wide instead of jumping if you have knee or ankle pain today.
Land softly; heavy landings load the knees and ankles.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Landing with locked knees, which sends the impact into the joints.
Letting the knees fall inward on landing.

exercises.name: Seated forward fold
how_to: Sit with your legs extended in front of you and your knees softly bent.
Hinge forward from your hips and let your spine round gently over your legs.
Rest your hands wherever they reach without straining, and let your head hang heavy.
Breathe slowly and let the stretch ease deeper on each out-breath.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Seated forward fold. Let the spine round gently over your legs and breathe slowly.
safety_notes: Bend the knees as much as you need; reaching your feet is not the point.
Ease off if you feel anything sharp behind the knees.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the feet to force more range.
Bouncing in and out of the stretch.

exercises.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
how_to: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front of you, knee above the ankle.
Draw your tailbone slightly under so your lower back does not arch.
Shift your weight gently forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the kneeling hip.
Hold and breathe slowly, then change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Kneeling hip flexor stretch. Tuck the tailbone under, then shift gently forward.
safety_notes: Put a cushion under the kneeling knee if it is uncomfortable.
Keep the front knee over the ankle rather than travelling past the toes.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis, which hides the stretch.
Pushing so far forward that the front knee collapses inward.

exercises.name: Supine chest opener
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Turn your palms upward and let the weight of your arms open your chest toward the floor.
Breathe slowly into the sides of your ribs and let your shoulders soften downward.
Stay for the full interval, letting each out-breath release a little more.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Chest opener. Arms wide, palms up, and let your shoulders soften toward the floor.
safety_notes: Bring the arms lower than shoulder height if the fronts of the shoulders pinch.
common_mistakes: Forcing the arms flat instead of letting them settle.
Arching the lower back to get the chest lower.

exercises.name: Reformer footwork, arches
how_to: Lie on the carriage with your head on the headrest and the arches of your feet hooked over the footbar.
Set a moderate spring load, typically two to three springs depending on your reformer.
Press the carriage away by straightening your legs, stopping just short of locking the knees.
Return slowly so the springs resist rather than pull you home.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Footwork on the arches. Press the carriage away, then return slowly against the springs.
safety_notes: Check the springs are attached before you load the carriage.
Keep the whole arch in contact with the bar so the ankle does not roll.
common_mistakes: Letting the heels drop below the bar, which changes the movement.
Allowing the carriage to close faster than you can control.

exercises.name: Reformer bridging on the footbar
how_to: Lie on the carriage with your feet flat on the footbar, knees bent and hip-width apart.
Use a heavier spring load so the carriage stays still while you work.
Press through your heels and peel your hips off the carriage one vertebra at a time.
Lower slowly from the top of the spine downward, keeping the carriage still throughout.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Reformer bridging. Peel the hips up one vertebra at a time, keeping the carriage still.
safety_notes: Use enough spring load that the carriage cannot slide under you.
Stop lifting at a straight line from shoulders to knees rather than pushing higher.
common_mistakes: Letting the carriage drift as the hips lift.
Over-arching at the top so the lower back takes the load.

exercises.name: Reformer supine arm press
how_to: Lie on the carriage with a strap in each hand and your arms reaching toward the ceiling.
Use a light spring load so your shoulders can stay soft and settled.
Press your arms down toward your hips, keeping your elbows long but not locked.
Return slowly to the ceiling, letting the springs resist the whole way.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Supine arm press. Press the straps down toward your hips, then return slowly.
safety_notes: Keep the straps under tension so they cannot snap slack.
Reduce the load if your shoulders lift toward your ears.
common_mistakes: Letting the ribs flare as the arms travel overhead.
Using so much spring that the shoulders grip.

exercises.name: Reformer mermaid
how_to: Sit sideways on the carriage with your shins folded to one side and one hand on the footbar.
Use a light spring load so the carriage moves easily under your hand.
Reach the other arm overhead and side-bend away from the bar, letting the carriage glide out.
Return to upright slowly, then change sides.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Mermaid. Reach one arm overhead and side-bend away as the carriage glides out.
safety_notes: Keep both hips on the carriage so the stretch stays in the side of the waist.
Ease off if you feel anything sharp in the ribs or lower back.
common_mistakes: Rotating the chest toward the floor instead of side-bending.
Letting the supporting shoulder collapse.

exercises.name: Reformer short box, round back
how_to: Sit on the short box with your feet secured under the strap and your knees softly bent.
Hold your arms forward at shoulder height and round your lower spine backward.
Roll back only as far as you can return from without pulling on the strap.
Curl forward again to upright, leading with the lower abdominals.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Short box, round back. Roll back through a rounded spine, then curl forward again.
safety_notes: Check the box is stable and the foot strap is secure before you start.
Roll back a smaller distance rather than hauling yourself up with the strap.
common_mistakes: Going back so far that the feet do the returning.
Losing the rounded spine so the lower back extends.

exercises.name: Reformer elephant
how_to: Stand on the carriage with your hands on the footbar and your feet flexed against the shoulder rests.
Use a moderate spring load and fold forward so your spine rounds and your hips stay high.
Press the carriage back a short way using your abdominals rather than your legs.
Draw it home slowly, keeping your hips high and your spine rounded throughout.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Elephant. Hips high, spine rounded, and move the carriage with your abdominals.
safety_notes: Keep the range short; a long press turns this into a hamstring stretch under load.
Come off the carriage if your wrists ache.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the legs so the abdominals do nothing.
Letting the spine flatten, which shifts the work into the lower back.

exercises.name: Reformer long stretch
how_to: Take a plank position with your hands on the footbar and your feet against the shoulder rests.
Use a moderate spring load so the carriage resists rather than runs away.
Hold one straight line from head to heels and let the carriage travel back a short distance.
Draw it home with your abdominals, keeping the line unbroken.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Long stretch. Hold one straight line and move the carriage a short way, then home.
safety_notes: Come out of the position the moment your hips sag or pike.
Keep the range short; a long carriage travel makes the plank impossible to hold.
Check the springs before you take weight on the bar.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop so the lower back takes the load.
Travelling so far that the shoulders pass in front of the wrists.

exercises.name: Reformer knee stretches, round back
how_to: Kneel on the carriage with your hands on the footbar and your feet against the shoulder rests.
Round your lower spine and draw your knees in toward your hands.
Press the carriage back a short distance using your abdominals, keeping the rounded shape.
Return slowly and keep the rhythm even rather than fast.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Knee stretches. Keep the spine rounded and move the carriage with your abdominals.
safety_notes: Stop if the rounded shape flattens; the lower back takes over immediately.
Put a pad under your knees if they are uncomfortable on the carriage.
common_mistakes: Losing the round back and arching instead.
Rushing so momentum moves the carriage.

exercises.name: Reformer teaser in straps
how_to: Lie on the carriage with both feet in the straps and a light to moderate spring load.
Extend your legs to about 45 degrees and reach your arms toward your feet.
Curl your spine off the carriage into a shallow V, balancing on the back of your pelvis.
Lower the spine and the legs together with control, keeping the straps under tension.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Reformer teaser. Curl into a shallow V, then lower spine and legs together.
safety_notes: Keep the straps under tension the whole time so they cannot snap slack.
Come down if the lower back takes over from the abdominals.
Bend the knees if you cannot lower with control.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the straps to get up rather than curling the spine.
Dropping out of the shape instead of lowering through it.

exercises.name: Elliptical warm-up glide
how_to: Step on with a light hold on the handles and stand tall over the pedals.
Set the resistance to the lowest setting that still feels connected rather than free-wheeling.
Glide at an easy pace where you could talk without noticing your breathing.
Build the cadence very gradually across the interval.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Easy glide. Light resistance, comfortable pace, breathing you barely notice.
safety_notes: Hold the handles until your stride feels settled.
common_mistakes: Starting at working intensity so the warm-up does no warming up.
Leaning weight onto the handles rather than standing over the pedals.

exercises.name: Elliptical spin-down
how_to: Drop the resistance to its lowest useful setting.
Keep striding at a slow, easy cadence and let your breathing settle.
Stand tall rather than sagging onto the handles.
Continue until your breathing is close to conversational again.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Spin down. Drop the resistance and stride easily while your breathing settles.
safety_notes: Do not stop abruptly after hard work; keep moving easily instead.
common_mistakes: Stepping off immediately after a hard interval.
Keeping the resistance high so the cool-down is still work.

exercises.name: Elliptical cadence build
how_to: Keep the resistance at your steady-state setting.
Start at a comfortable stride rate and lift the cadence slightly every half minute or so.
Keep your torso quiet; the change should come from your legs, not your shoulders.
Settle back to your usual cadence at the end of the interval.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Cadence build. Same resistance, lift the stride rate a little at a time.
safety_notes: Back off the cadence if your feet start slapping the pedals.
Ease off if you feel light-headed.
common_mistakes: Raising the resistance instead of the cadence.
Bouncing the upper body as the stride quickens.

exercises.name: Elliptical reverse stride
how_to: Slow to almost a stop, then begin striding backward with a light hold on the handles.
Keep the same steady-state resistance and a slightly slower cadence than forward.
Stay tall and keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Return to forward striding before the interval ends if your balance wavers.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Reverse stride. Slow down first, then stride backward, staying tall.
safety_notes: Change direction only from a near-stop; switching at speed is how ankles get twisted.
Hold the handles until the backward stride feels settled.
common_mistakes: Reversing at full speed rather than slowing first.
Sitting back into the hips so the knees fall inward.

exercises.name: Elliptical arms-and-legs surge
how_to: Take hold of the moving handles rather than the fixed bars.
Raise the resistance one step above your steady setting.
Drive with your arms and legs together at an effort of six to seven out of ten.
Return to the fixed bars and an easy pace when the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Drive the moving handles with your arms as well as your legs.
safety_notes: Keep your shoulders down rather than shrugged as you pull.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Yanking with the arms so the shoulders take over from the legs.
Letting the torso rock side to side.

exercises.name: Elliptical strong effort
how_to: Raise the resistance one step above your steady-state setting.
Stride briskly at an effort where you can still speak a short sentence.
Keep standing tall and let your heels stay in contact with the pedals.
Drop back to your steady setting as soon as the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Strong effort. One step more resistance, brisk stride, six out of ten.
safety_notes: Choose the effort yourself; there is no target speed to chase.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Going so hard that the interval cannot be finished.
Leaning on the handles once the effort rises.

exercises.name: Elliptical high-resistance push
how_to: Raise the resistance well above your steady setting, until the cadence drops noticeably.
Hold the fixed bars lightly and drive down through each pedal.
Work at an effort of eight to nine out of ten, where speech is a word or two at most.
Reduce the resistance immediately when the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: High resistance push. Drive down through each pedal, eight to nine out of ten.
safety_notes: Reduce the resistance if your knees ache or your hips rock.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Hauling on the handles to move resistance the legs cannot.
Holding the effort past the point where the stride becomes uneven.

exercises.name: Elliptical hands-free stride
how_to: Settle into your steady-state resistance and a comfortable cadence.
Let go of the handles and hold your arms lightly by your sides.
Keep your ribs stacked over your hips and your stride even.
Take hold of the handles again the moment your balance wavers.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Hands-free stride. Let go of the handles and keep your ribs stacked over your hips.
safety_notes: Keep one hand near a handle at all times so you can catch yourself.
Skip this movement if your balance is at all unsteady today.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to stay upright, which shortens the stride.
Letting the cadence rise so far that balance goes.

exercises.name: Easy spin
how_to: Set the saddle so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke.
Add just enough resistance that the flywheel feels connected rather than free.
Spin at a comfortable cadence where your breathing barely changes.
Sit tall with your hands resting lightly on the bars.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Easy spin. Light resistance, comfortable cadence, breathing you barely notice.
safety_notes: Never pedal with no resistance; the flywheel will drive your legs.
common_mistakes: Removing all resistance so the pedals run away.
Starting at working intensity during a warm-up.

exercises.name: Warm-up roll
how_to: Sit tall with a light hold on the bars and a low resistance setting.
Spin at a steady, easy cadence and let your legs find a smooth circle.
Add a small amount of resistance partway through so the effort rises gently.
Keep your hips still in the saddle throughout.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Warm-up roll. Smooth circles, easy resistance, adding a little partway through.
safety_notes: Keep a little resistance on at all times so the pedals stay under control.
common_mistakes: Rocking the hips at a very high cadence.
Adding so much resistance that the warm-up becomes the work.

exercises.name: Recovery spin
how_to: Reduce the resistance to well below your working setting.
Spin at a light, steady cadence and let your breathing come back down.
Sit tall and unclench your hands and jaw.
Keep moving for the whole interval rather than coasting to a stop.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Recovery spin. Light resistance, keep the legs turning, let your breathing come down.
safety_notes: Keep pedalling rather than stopping dead after a hard effort.
common_mistakes: Leaving the resistance high so the recovery is not a recovery.
Stopping entirely between hard intervals.

exercises.name: Seated tempo
how_to: Add resistance until holding a cadence around 85 takes real effort.
Stay seated and tall, with your hands light on the bars.
Work at an effort of six to seven out of ten, where sentences become short.
Keep the effort even for the whole interval rather than surging.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Seated tempo. Steady and strong, six to seven out of ten.
safety_notes: Drop the resistance if your hips begin rocking in the saddle.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Starting too hard and fading before the interval ends.
Gripping the bars hard enough to hunch the shoulders.

exercises.name: Standing climb
how_to: Add enough resistance to stand against comfortably before you rise.
Come out of the saddle with your hips back over the saddle nose and hands wide on the bars.
Press through the whole pedal circle at a cadence around 60 to 70.
Sit back down before your form breaks rather than at the last moment.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Standing climb. Hips back, wide hands, press through the whole pedal circle.
safety_notes: Never stand with light resistance; you will lose control of the pedals.
Sit down as soon as your knees start to wobble inward.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Standing too far forward so weight lands on the arms.
Bouncing rather than pressing smoothly.

exercises.name: High-cadence surge
how_to: Keep a moderate resistance — enough to stay connected at speed.
Stay seated and lift the cadence above 100 while keeping your hips quiet.
Work at an effort of eight out of ten, breathing hard but in rhythm.
Drop back to your steady cadence when the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: High cadence surge. Stay seated, lift the cadence, keep the hips quiet.
safety_notes: Reduce the cadence if your hips start bouncing in the saddle.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Dropping the resistance so low that the flywheel drives the legs.
Bouncing in the saddle rather than spinning smoothly.

exercises.name: Seated to standing jumps
how_to: Set a moderate to heavy resistance so you have something to stand against.
Ride seated at a controlled cadence, then rise smoothly out of the saddle.
Hold the standing position for a few pedal strokes, then sit back down without dropping.
Keep the resistance and the cadence steady across both positions.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Jumps. Rise smoothly out of the saddle, then sit back down without dropping.
safety_notes: Never make the transition with light resistance; the pedals will run away from you.
Skip this movement if you have knee or hip pain today.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Dropping heavily back into the saddle.
Letting the cadence spike on the way up.

exercises.name: Standing sprint, heavy gear
how_to: Add resistance until standing feels like climbing rather than spinning.
Rise out of the saddle with your hips over the pedals and hands wide.
Drive as hard as you can hold for the whole interval, around nine out of ten.
Sit and spin easy the instant the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Heavy standing sprint. Hips over the pedals, drive hard, nine out of ten.
safety_notes: Build up to this over several weeks rather than starting here.
Skip it entirely if you have knee or hip pain today.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Holding the sprint past the point where form collapses.
Bouncing the hips instead of staying centred over the pedals.

exercises.name: Single-leg focus
how_to: Set a moderate resistance and settle into a steady seated cadence.
Shift your attention to one leg and concentrate on pulling through the back of the stroke.
Keep both feet on the pedals; the other leg keeps turning but does less.
Change the emphasis to the other leg partway through the interval.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Single-leg focus. Concentrate on pulling one leg through the back of the stroke.
safety_notes: Keep both feet on the pedals throughout; unclipping mid-interval is how falls happen.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Letting the cadence collapse while concentrating.
Rocking the hips toward the working leg.

exercises.name: Smooth pedalling drill
how_to: Set a light resistance and sit tall with your hands resting on the bars.
Spin at a comfortable cadence and picture your feet tracing an even circle.
Concentrate on removing the dead spots at the top and bottom of each stroke.
Keep your hips completely still in the saddle.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Smooth circles. Trace an even circle with each foot and keep your hips still.
safety_notes: Keep some resistance on so the flywheel cannot drive your legs.
common_mistakes: Stamping down on the pedals rather than turning circles.
Raising the cadence until the hips start to rock.

exercises.name: Reformer pelvic tilts
how_to: Lie on the carriage with your feet flat on the footbar and a heavier spring load so the carriage stays still.
Find a neutral pelvis, so your lower back is neither arched nor pressed hard down.
Breathe out and tilt your pelvis so your lower back flattens gently toward the carriage.
Breathe in and return to neutral, moving only the pelvis.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Pelvic tilts. Flatten the lower back gently as you breathe out, then return to neutral.
safety_notes: Use enough spring load that the carriage cannot slide while you work.
common_mistakes: Pushing through the feet so the carriage moves instead of the pelvis.
Squeezing the glutes to tilt rather than using the abdominals.

exercises.name: Reformer spine stretch forward
how_to: Sit on the carriage facing the footbar with your legs apart and your hands on the bar.
Use a light spring load so the carriage moves with your control rather than pulling you.
Sit tall, then round your spine forward from the top, letting the carriage glide away.
Restack the spine from the base upward to return to sitting tall.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Spine stretch forward. Round from the top, then restack the spine from the base upward.
safety_notes: Bend your knees if your hamstrings limit sitting upright.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hips instead of articulating the spine.
Pushing the bar away with the arms rather than moving from the spine.

exercises.name: Elliptical sustained hard effort
how_to: Raise the resistance two steps above your steady-state setting.
Hold a strong, even cadence with a light hold on the fixed bars.
Work at an effort of eight out of ten and hold it for the whole interval without surging.
Reduce the resistance and stride easily as soon as the interval ends.
exercises.spoken_instruction: Sustained hard effort. Hold eight out of ten evenly, no surging.
safety_notes: Reduce the effort if you cannot hold the cadence steady.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
common_mistakes: Surging early and fading before the interval ends.
Leaning weight onto the handles once the effort rises.
